title: Writing box with decoration of seven deer in autumn grasses
medium: Gold maki-e, inlaid mother-of-pearl, and lead on black lacquer

altText: A black lacquer box decorated in gold and shimmering inlay with a design of deer among autumn grasses.

context: A writing box made in Japan in the 19th century, during the Edo period. It is black lacquer decorated with gold maki-e, mother-of-pearl inlay, and lead, and its design shows seven deer among autumn grasses. Writing boxes held an inkstone, ink stick, brushes, and water dropper.

descriptions.k: This is a shiny black box with a picture on it. Deer walk among autumn grasses. The picture is made with gold. Some parts sparkle like shells. What do you think is inside this box?
descriptions.g12: This black box from Japan was made to hold writing tools. Seven deer stand among tall grasses on the lid, and the design is made of gold and shiny shell. The black background makes them glow. Can you count the deer? Where do you think they are looking?
descriptions.g35: This is a writing box from Japan, made to hold an inkstone, ink stick, and brushes. Its black lacquer is decorated with gold powder in a technique called maki-e, plus shiny mother-of-pearl. The design shows seven deer among autumn grasses. Look at how the gold stands out against the black. Why might a maker decorate a box for writing with deer and autumn plants?
descriptions.g68: Made in the 19th century, this writing box uses maki-e, in which designs are drawn in lacquer and gold powder is sprinkled on before it sets. Mother-of-pearl and lead add other shines. Deer among autumn grasses is a classic combination in Japanese poetry and art, so the box may call up the season and its mood. The dark ground sets off the shimmering design. How do you think the box looked when opened by lamplight?
descriptions.g910: The box transforms a functional object into a small landscape. Gold maki-e, mother-of-pearl, and lead create varied reflective effects against black lacquer, which makes the deer and grasses seem to glow. Deer among autumn plants are a motif with strong poetic associations in Japanese culture, though how a specific owner read them is not recorded. Consider how a writing box, linked to literacy and refinement, uses imagery and luxury materials to signal taste.
descriptions.g1112: This writing box exemplifies how Edo-period lacquer fused function, craft, and cultural reference. Gold maki-e, inlaid mother-of-pearl, and lead produce layered optical effects on black lacquer, yielding a design that changes with light. The pairing of deer and autumn grasses draws on a long poetic and pictorial tradition, which gives the object a literary resonance, though individual meanings can only be inferred. Because the box was meant to be handled and opened, display behind glass reduces our access to part of its intended experience. How do material and motif shape meaning?

teacherNote.context: A 19th-century Edo-period writing box with gold maki-e, mother-of-pearl, and lead on black lacquer. Writing boxes held the tools for calligraphy.
directions: Let students plan a decorated lid for a pencil box using only a limited palette.
Ask students to pair an animal with a season they associate with it, then justify the pairing.
Compare with the other writing boxes in the archive and discuss how each chooses a motif.
